newsitem.title: MEXICO: Police, officials sentenced for Mexico massacre.
newsitem.headline: Police, officials sentenced for Mexico massacre.

text.p: A judge in the southwestern state of Guerrero on Friday sentenced 28 police officers to prison terms for their part in a massacre of 17 peasants more than two years ago.
The state Superior Court also fined and sentenced nine high-level government officials, including an ex-director of the state police, for their part in the incident.
The 17 peasants were killed in a massacre at Aguas Blancas in June 1995 by police officers who opened fire on dozens of peasants riding in the back of trucks.
The sentences for the condemned police officers ran from two years to 24 years in prison for murder, abuse of authority and bodily harm. The police officers also were fined a little more than $1,000.
Two of the former government officials also were charged with actions that did not conform with their public positions and had their prison terms extended to 26 1/2 years.
The attack outraged Mexicans as video footage showed police officers placing guns in the hands of their victims in an attempt to show the police had fired in self-defence.
Ruben Figeroa, then governor of the poor state, was later forced to resign over the incident.
